newsitem.title: HONG KONG: March 14 start for China Airlines Miami service.
newsitem.headline: March 14 start for China Airlines Miami service.

text.p: China Airlines (CAL) is to launch its first freighter service to Miami on March 14, a company statement said.

Industry sources said approval for the new route has been awaited for more than two years but the log jam was cleared in January when Taiwan gave Federal Express Corp, the go-ahead for a new sorting centre in Taipei.

On February 28, the U.S. Department of Transportation said the U.S. and Taiwan had reached an "open skies" agreement allowing carriers from each country to fly to any city in the other country as often as they wish.
In addition the department said the pact allows airlines from each country to fly on to third countries and to market their services jointly in code-sharing agreements.
CAL's Boeing 747-200 service will initially be once weekly but that is expected to quickly be stepped up to at least three times weekly.

"As the first Asian carrier to introduce direct service to Miami, CAL provides excellent connections for air freight transportation between Latin America and Asia. It is believed that trade and air cargo between those two parts of the world will grow rapidly once the air bridge is open," the CAL statement said.
CAL also operates freighter services to Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Chicago and Dallas.

CAL's director of cargo sales and marketing, Peter Yap, said recently that CAL has good relations with a number of Central American airlines and Miami is an important link in his airline's growth strategy which has seen cargo revenue increase by around 14 per cent over the past decade. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
